task.title: Reconcile merged nonterminal L12 rows
task.phase: Twelve Loop Remediation / Wave 0 Closeout Reconcile

scope.owned_layer: Inventory of merged-but-nonterminal L12/SUP-L12 canonical rows, immutable task-brief-shaped merged evidence for the one stranded row, and a verifier that runs the governed reconcile gate.
not_changing: any canonical status, archive, or activity file
the canonical rows of L12-FLEET-STATUS-SYNC-001 and SUP-L12-FLEET-RUNTIME-RELIABILITY-20260729

method: PR-side: gh pr list --state merged --limit 200, map task/<id> head branch to a canonical row, keep rows that are neither done nor archived
commit-side: git log --grep '<task-id>' origin/dev for every nonterminal row in ai-status.json

design_decisions.decision: store the merged reconcile evidence outside .orchestrator/task-briefs/
design_decisions.why: supervisor.py lists .orchestrator/task-briefs/ in _REUSABLE_DIRTY_PREFIXES and regenerates those files from the live row via _generated_worker_task_brief on each dispatch, rewriting the '- Status:' line. validate_merged_done_evidence requires the on-disk file to be byte-identical to its merged commit and to contain a literal '^- Status: review_approved$', so a brief under that prefix is guaranteed to break both gates once the supervisor touches it. The gate imposes no directory requirement.
design_decisions.observable_now: the live command root shows modified .orchestrator/task-briefs/*.md files

design_decisions.decision: produce evidence for one row, not three
design_decisions.why: reconcile_merged_done archives the row and is a recovery path. L12-FLEET-STATUS-SYNC-001 has a live closeout PR whose trailers already match, and SUP-L12-FLEET-RUNTIME-RELIABILITY-20260729 is mid-review with an open PR; reconciling either would archive work that still has a correct route, and would kill the reviewer's ability to act on the open PR.

design_decisions.decision: cite the reviewed head 7b68b423 as RECONCILE_DELIVERY_COMMIT rather than the merge commit
design_decisions.why: #4330 was merged with a true merge commit, not a squash, so the reviewed head is itself reachable from origin/dev and binds the delivery to the exact commit the reviewer approved. The merge commit d9cbbbfa is recorded too and also satisfies the ancestry gate.

operator_recovery.precondition: $PANTHEON_COMMAND_ROOT must be promoted to a dev commit containing the evidence file; validate_merged_done_evidence resolves RECONCILE_EVIDENCE_FILE against the command root, which is detached at PANTHEON_COMMAND_RUNTIME_SHA
operator_recovery.reviewer_reassignment_note: the evidence reviewer Claude2 equals the canonical row reviewer, so _verified_reviewer_reassignment is not exercised and no exact task_reassigned audit event is needed

integrity.binding_rule: artifacts are bound by content digest, not by branch commit SHA: auto_integrator rebases task branches onto the dev tip and rewrites every branch SHA while leaving artifact trees byte-identical, which silently orphans any SHA recorded here

externally_verifiable_facts: the reconcile evidence blob digest above is what Human/Ops must see on dev before running the recovery

evidence_policy.mutation_rule: the reconcile/ file is immutable once merged: validate_merged_done_evidence compares it byte-for-byte against its merged commit, so any later edit invalidates the recovery until a new evidence commit is supplied
evidence_policy.no_pr_head_facts_pre_merge: this manifest deliberately records no PR head SHA for its own delivery. The commit that recorded such a head would become the new head, making the field stale on landing; artifact digests above carry the identity instead
evidence_policy.reviewer_verdict_location: the reviewer's decision is recorded by the governed approve command as a commit status on the exact reviewed head, not transcribed into this manifest. This row is not a loop-autopilot task, so loop_done_guardrail.check_task imposes no record_log verdict requirement and no transcription commit is needed
evidence_policy.self_attestation_guard: the positive verification run is meaningless without the four negative controls above; each returns exit 1 with a distinct governed gate message, demonstrating the verifier reads its inputs rather than printing success
